legend: Cords and sinusoids of the spleen are infiltrated by a monotonous population of neoplastic lymphoid cells with medium-sized nuclei and a moderate rim of pale cytoplasm.

legend: The bone marrow is usually hypercellular, with neoplastic cells infiltrating sinusoids.

legend: Lymphoma cells infiltrate and expand the liver sinusoids (H&E). Inset: the lymphoma cells are positive for T-cell marker CD7.

diagnosis: Hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma involving bone marrow
legend: The bone marrow biopsy specimen is hypercellular, with lymphoma cells involving sinusoids (H&E). Inset: top left: aspirate smear showing lymphoma cells with nucleoli (Wright–Giemsa). Inset: bottom right: the lymphoma cells expanded sinusoids and are highlighted by expression of the T-cell marker CD3.
The cords and sinuses of the splenic red pulp are expanded and replaced by lymphoma cells. Inset: the lymphoma cells are positive for the T-cell marker CD3.
A At low magnification, the splenic red pulp is expanded and appears hypercellular; the white pulp is atrophic.
